newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Uighurs could be behind Beijing bombings - exiles.
newsitem.headline: Uighurs could be behind Beijing bombings - exiles.

text.p: An exile group in the Central Asian state of Kazakhstan said on Monday ethnic Uighur separatists could have been behind last week's bus bombings in the Chinese capital Peking.

"We do not rule out that this action was taken by separatist groups from Urumqi," Modan Mukhlisi, spokesman for the Uighur separatist United National Revolutionary Front of East Turkestan, told Reuters.

Urumqi is the regional capital of China's vast northwestern province of Xinjiang, where some ethnic Uighur groups, a Turkic-speaking Moslem people, have carried out bombings and assassinations in their struggle for independence from China.

Information from the remote region of mountain and desert is difficult to verify. Uighur exiles themselves admit to poor communications with separatist groups across the Chinese-Kazakh border in Xinjiang.
"State television in Urumqi also softened its line against Uighur separatists in broadcasts on Saturday after the bombings," said Mukhlisi.

He said the broadcasts showed that the Beijing bombings had prompted local Chinese authorities to have second thoughts about cracking down on Uighur separatists following bloody riots and a spate of arrests in Xinjiang last month.
"They (Beijing) must understand that more repression and arrests will be answered with more radical actions," said Mukhlisi.
He said a group of young Uighur men from the region's southern town of Khotan had headed for the nearby mountains to form a paramilitary group to fight for independence.
Beijing Mayor Jia Qinglin said on Monday there was no evidence to link bombings in the Chinese capital last week with earlier attacks in the restive region of Xinjiang.
"So far we have uncovered no connection," Jia told reporters when asked if the bomb attacks in Beijing and Xinjiang were connected.
But China's police called on hotels in Beijing to tighten security the same day.
Exile groups in Kazakhstan, however, have been at pains to distance themselves from separatist violence in Xinjiang.
China has put strong diplomatic pressure on the neighbouring Central Asian states of Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan not to aid the Uighur separatists.
"The allegations that Uighur exiles residing in Kazakhstan are behind the bombings in Beijing is not true," Kakharman Khozhamberdi, head of Kazakhstan's Regional Uighur Association, told Reuters.
